title: Trade Policy Activity Index
text:
Trade Policy Activity Index
    
    
    
      A novel composite indicator measuring the evolution of global trade policy
      since the Global Financial Crisis, covering 197 countries and territories.
    
  




  
    
      ✓  Updated through October 2025
      
        
        Samuele Centorrino  ·  Antonia Diakantoni  · 
        Alexander Keck  ·  Michele Ruta  · 
        Monika Sztajerowska  ·  Yuting Wei
      
    
  





  
    About the TPA Index

    
      The Trade Policy Activity (TPA) Index is a composite indicator of global trade policy
      activity, constructed using a Dynamic Factor Model applied to comprehensive data on
      trade policy interventions across 197 countries and territories since January 2010.
      The index documents a structural shift around 2019, reflecting a substantial and
      persistent expansion in the use of trade policy measures globally.
    

    
      
        How has it been constructed?
        
          The TPA Index is estimated using a Dynamic Factor Model (DFM) on a large
          cross-section of monthly trade policy intervention data sourced from the
          Global Trade Alert (GTA) and WTO databases. The model extracts a common
          factor from the co-movement across country- and measure-level series,
          interpreted as aggregate global trade policy activity. All series are
          smoothed using a three-month moving average and normalized so that the
          average equals zero over January 2010–December 2011. The index additionally
          incorporates Mixed Data Sampling (MIDAS) regressions on high-frequency GTA
          data to enable real-time nowcasting of trade policy shifts.
        
      
      
        What does it include?
        
          The dataset provides eight monthly series from January 2010 to October 2025:
          a Global Factor (baseline worldwide index);
          a Facilitating sub-index (trade-liberalizing measures and rollbacks);
          an Other sub-index (non-facilitating measures including tariff
          increases, bans, quotas, and subsidies);
          a Restrictive sub-index (trade-restricting subset of Other);
          a Remaining other sub-index (largely subsidies and industrial policy);
          G20 and Non-G20 economy indices;
          and a GDP-weighted index using pre-sample GDP shares (2005–2009)
          as time-invariant weights.
        
      
    

    
      
        Why is it different from other measures?
        
          Existing trade policy measures tend to focus on tariffs alone or rely on
          annual survey data. The TPA Index covers the full range of policy instruments —
          tariffs, non-tariff barriers, export restrictions, and industrial policy — at
          monthly frequency across a near-global sample. Its DFM framework extracts the
          underlying co-movement rather than simply counting interventions, and the MIDAS
          nowcasting component enables real-time monitoring well ahead of official data releases.
        
      
      
        What are the key findings?
        
          The TPA Index identifies a structural break around 2019 — a persistent expansion
          in global trade policy activity departing from the post-GFC baseline. Beyond this
          trend, the index captures cyclical spikes during the 2018–19 US–China trade war,
          COVID-19 supply chain disruptions, and the post-2022 wave of industrial policy.
          G20 and non-G20 economies differ significantly in the timing, intensity, and
          instrument mix of their trade policy responses.
